articleTitle: Dynamic Spectrum Sharing Based on the Rentable NFT Standard ERC4907
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Centralized Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS) faces challenges like data security, high management costs, and limited scalability. To address these issues, a blockchain-based DSS scheme has been proposed in this paper. First, we utilize the ERC4907 standard to mint Non-Fungible Spectrum Tokens (NFSTs) that serve as unique identifiers for spectrum resources and facilitate renting. Next, we develop a smart contract for NFST auctions, ensuring secure spectrum transactions through the auction process. Lastly, we create a Web3 spectrum auction platform where users can access idle spectrum data and participate in auctions for NFST leases corresponding to the available spectrum. Experimental results demonstrate that our NFST, designed according to the ERC4907 standard, effectively meets users' secure and efficient DSS requirements, making it a feasible solution.

articleTitle: Diesel Engine Monitoring and Diagnostics Based on Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper addresses the vital requirements for automated diesel engine monitoring in unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) to prevent potential malfunctions from affecting navigation. We propose an efficient audio pattern recognition system employing artificial neural networks (ANN). The end-to-end model identifies anomalies in engine audio, simplifying the monitoring system and enabling online identification. Data collected from diesel engine USVs contribute to a comprehensive audio dataset. Comparative analysis involving ResNet50, MobileNet, and Vision Transformer (ViT) models on the spectrogram dataset is conducted, with a focus on classification accuracy. ViT outperforms, achieving superior accuracy of 98.2% and a real-time processing speed exceeding 14 frames per second on the engine audio dataset. This study introduces an effective solution for real-time acoustic monitoring, especially beneficial for remote control and all-weather monitoring in USVs.

articleTitle: Joint Source-Channel Coding base on DL for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Image Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Traditional image transmission solutions incorporate source coding to minimize redundant information, addressing bandwidth and power constraints. Following this, channel coding is applied to introduce redundancy, ensuring the efficacy of data transmission. However, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) encounter challenges such as limited signal coverage, poor channel conditions, and constraints on transmission bandwidth and energy during wireless image transmission. The utilization of traditional source-channel concatenated coding for data transmission incurs a high cost. To tackle this challenge, this paper proposes a Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) image transmission solution based on deep learning. This approach directly maps image pixels to complex-valued channels, thereby reducing the overall cost of end-to-end transmission. Furthermore, an optimized JSCC method is introduced, integrating adaptive attention mechanisms, channel estimation, and channel equalization algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method not only outperforms traditional concatenated transmission schemes but also enhances the performance of JSCC in terms of transmission quality.

articleTitle: SSFP: A Structured Stripe-Filter Pruning Method for Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Network pruning has gained popularity for reducing storage and computational requirements in deep neural network models. However, common pruning techniques focus on the single granularity without sufficiently exploring collaborative research on different granularity levels. In order to explore the combination of different pruning granularities while effectively compressing the network in a structured manner, this paper proposes a structured stripe-filter pruning method (SSFP) that combines filter and stripe pruning. The fine-grained is embedded within the architecture of coarse-grained pruning, employing a mixed compression strategy with two pruning modules to accomplish pruning tasks. Experiments demonstrate better model compression results than the comparison techniques in the VGG-16 and RESNET-56 convolutional neural networks. When applying SSFP to VGG-16, FLOPs is reduced by 70.1 %, the total number of parameters is reduced by 93.5%, and the accuracy of CIFAR-I0 is improved from 93.40% to 93.63%.

articleTitle: Research on Side-Scan Sonar Target Detection Technology based on Improved Yolov5
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In recent years, the target detection of side-scan sonar image is an important part of underwater target search, ocean mapping and Marine geological detection, so improving the target detection accuracy of sonar image is of great significance for underwater detection. Aiming at the low target detection accuracy of side-scan sonar images, this paper conducted a target detection test on side-scan sonar image data based on Yolov5 algorithm, used existing side-scan sonar equipment to collect side-scan sonar images to build side-scan sonar data set, and used Yolov5 algorithm to study its target detection technology. The experimental results show that the method can detect the target image with high precision, and the target detection accuracy reaches 98.6%, which can complete the target detection task of underwater specific target with high precision and all-round in the actual hydrological environment.

articleTitle: Hybrid Adjacency Representation for Few-Shot Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: With the widespread use of large language models, image parsing remains a hot issue in the field. Although the deep learning method can solve some problems in an extent, specially domains with small dataset are hard to apply. This paper is dedicated to image classification using few-shot learning methods. First, it utilizes a basic framework for the entry classes of support and query sets, where the query sets are distinguished by the similarity of the class attribute. A hybrid adjacency representation(HAR) composed of a global self-similarity descriptor (GSSD) and a cross-similarity descriptor (CSD) is proposed. The GSSD is used to extract structural patterns from query and support sets, then transform the base representations into its self-correlation tensor. The CSD is adapted to aggregate the selected features of GSSD to promote the similarity of visual appearance. Lastly, the ablation studies and the extensive experiments show competitive results over the state-of-the-art methods on the benchmark.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Network Architecture for Sonar Image Denoising Based on U-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: With the increase of marine activities, underwater target detection has become a key technology for the development of marine resources and maintenance of rights and interests. Due to the complexity of underwater environment, the multiplicative scattering noise in sonar images often affects the accuracy of detection algorithms. Meanwhile, in order to solve the problem of no clean reference image pairing, a two-stage U-Net denoising algorithm (TUDA) is proposed in this paper. First, the method in this paper uses a two-stage architecture to gradually learn the sonar denoising features in the ideal state. Then, the residual encoder-decoder architecture learns the contextual features, and the information exchange between different stages is enhanced by passing the features from the previous stage to the next stage for aggregation through the cross-stage feature fusion and supervised attention module. The experimental results on sonar datasets show that TUDA achieves better results on the no-reference image quality evaluation metrics NIQE, BRISQUE when compared with the traditional and state-of-the-art methods. Therefore, TUDA can better retain the image's texture information and edge structure features while denoising, showing better visual effects.

articleTitle: Research on the Preparation and Temperature Sensing Property of In-Fiber Coupled WGM Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In this study, we design a temperature sensor based on whispering-gallery-mode (WGM), which is constructed from a single-mode fiber (SMF) and two varieties of multimode fiber (MMF) with varying core diameters. A barium titanate microsphere is placed in an arc cavity etched by hydrofluoric acid at the end of the MMF to excite WGMs. The quality factor is calculated as 1.31 X 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>• In the temperature range of 25°C to 50°C, the sensitivity of the sensor is 4.84 pm/rC. This paper provides a strong WGM excitation scheme, which resolves the vulnerability issue commonly seen in the customary WGM coupling structure and is an ideal selection for optical fiber sensing.

articleTitle: Restoration of Distorted Laser-Spot Image Based on Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: We introduce the generative adversarial networks (GANs) into the application of the free-space laser communication, performing the laser-spot image restoration with the computervision method. After the training of our model is completed, the average Pearson correlation coefficient, average peak signal-to-noise ratio and mean-square-error of the generated restored laser spot image reach 0.964, 27.713dB and 0.003, respectively. According to the numerical results, the GAN method could effectively resist the interference of atmospheric turbulence, and accurately restore the amplitude distribution of the laser captured from the free-space channel.

articleTitle: Automatic Multi-Constraint Placement of Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Every printed circuit board (PCB) has a complex and changeable placement area. Many physical restrictions bring about constraints in PCB design so that design of PCB automatic placement algorithms shall be greatly challenging. An automatic multi-constraint placement method of PCB that is based on the B*-tree and simulated annealing algorithm is put forward here to reduce the total cost of placement area and HPWL. Thus, placement resources can be optimally utilized. Our main work is as follows: (1) An internal placement strategy that enables IC chip components to be placed preferentially inside the PCB while auxiliary components connected to them are placed close to each other is designed; (2) An obstacle block generation algorithm that is based on area division is applied to place irregular outlines; and (3) Double-layer placement algorithm that is applied to be away from restricted areas for components in double-layer PCB placement. Experimental results on some industrial cases show that our method can inexpensively complete multi-constraint PCB placement.

articleTitle: Optimization of Acoustic Energy Flux Method Based on Single Pressure Gradient Vector Hydrophone
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In the case of a single pressure-gradient vector hydrophone, if the ratio of its diameter to wavelength fails to satisfy the engineering approximation conditions, the direct calculation of the angle through the arc tangent method for directional of arrival (DOA) estimation will result in a significant estimation error. While using the modified sound intensity method to correct its array flow pattern, a higher signal-to-noise ratio is required. This paper presents the upper limit for the diameter-to-wavelength ratio and introduces a refined approach for estimating the direction of arrival (DOA) by employing a mapping function replacement the modified sound intensity method. The proposed method improves the performance of the estimation of DOA based on a single pressure-gradient vector hydrophone, particularly in scenarios with low signal-to-noise ratios. Simultaneously, this method serves to broaden the applicable frequency range for azimuth angle estimation. The simulation findings provide empirical evidence supporting the efficacy and superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Automatic Placement of PCB Functional Modules Based on Regional Division
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: The placement of printed circuit board (PCB) functional modules presents unique constraints, which pose great challenges for automatic placement algorithms. In consideration of the modular nature of PCBs, we propose an automatic placement method for PCB functional modules based on regional division. Our work involves the following steps: (1) Constructing and analyzing a model of PCB functional module placement; (2) Dividing the placement area and assigning priority to components; (3) Utilizing the relay-race algorithm (RRA) to achieve rapid convergence of the placement algorithm. Experimental results from industrial cases demonstrate that our method can effectively enhance the efficiency of placement operations and achieve better wire length for nets while meeting the specifications for PCB functional module placement.

articleTitle: Noise Leakage Shaping Technique with Auxiliary Digital Noise Coupling in CT MASH DSM
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a continuous-time (CT) multi-stage noise shaping (MASH) delta -sigma modulator (DSM) with noise leakage shaping for high resolution applications. By an auxiliary digital noise coupling loop, the quantization noise leakage is significantly alleviated in the proposed CT MASH architecture. Therefore, this technique reduces requirements of operational amplifiers without trading the resolution loss. Furthermore, this technique allows using intrinsically linear single-bit quantizer in the first stage and high resolution multi-bit quantizer in the later stages, thus the proposed CT MASH enjoys benefits provided by multi-bit quantization and avoids using any complex DAC linearization technique. Mathematical analysis and further simulation results are provided to prove the effectiveness of the proposed architecture and its high potential for high resolution applications.

articleTitle: M-Ary Underwater Acoustic Spread Spectrum Communication Receiver Based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: The spread spectrum communication method is widely used in underwater transmission of military and commercial information due to its confidentiality properties, but it is affected by ocean noise and variable underwater sound fields. This paper proposes a Transformer-based underwater acoustic signal receiver called UWASiT(Underwater Acoustic Signal Transformer) to reduce the communication bit error rate. Two different water channel datas are used for UWASiT training to improve the generalization ability for unknown data. The UWASiT designed in this paper is used to joint channel estimation, channel equalization and signal detection to demodulate underwater acoustic spread spectrum signals. In order to test the performance of this Transformer-based deep neural network model, BOLLHOP is used to simulate the impulse response of the underwater acoustic channel, and the bit error rates under different signal-to-noise ratios are compared with other neural networks. The UWASiT neural network model designed in this paper has significant anti-noise and anti-fading capability, and has a lower bit error rate, which provides an new idea for the design of underwater acoustic spread spectrum communication scheme.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Floating-Point Transcendental Function Processor Based on RISC- V Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Floating-point (FP) transcendental function operations are widely used in deep learning, remote sensing radar, and other engineering and application fields. Computing these FP functions through integer arithmetic logic units requires a large number of clock cycles. Coordinate rotation digital computer (CORDIC) is one of the commonly used algorithms for hardware computation of transcendental functions. The high radix adaptive CORDIC (HCORDIC) algorithm, which has the advantages of fewer iterations and faster convergence, is implemented using the IEEE-754 FP standard. Due to the advantages of flexibility, customization, and scalability of the RISC- V instruction set architecture (ISA), a processor based on the RISC- V FP transcendental function extension is proposed. The proposed processor has been implemented on Xilinx Zynq X7CZ020 FPGA. The result shows that the processor executes transcendental functions at least 100 times faster than without the accelerator. The calculation accuracy ranges from 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> to 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> and the maximum operating frequency is 201.13 MHz, making it highly valuable in engineering applications.

articleTitle: Evaluating Results of PCB Routing Based on the Two-Dimensional Entropy Model
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: With the development of automatic placement and routing technologies of printed circuit board (PCB), it takes a long time to perform the subjective evaluation by engineers, and the evaluation process has become a bottleneck procedure of the automatic design process of PCB. In this paper, a two-dimensional entropy model is introduced for the first time to evaluate the quality of local routing with the characteristics of bus wiring, and two metrics are proposed for evaluation of the routing order and the routing aggregation, respectively. Experimental results manifest that for all test cases, the proposed indexes based on the two-dimensional entropy model can effectively identify the aggregation level and the order level of the local routing results without considering electrical characteristics and other constraints.

articleTitle: Blind Detection of Non-cooperative Communication Signals Based on Feature Dimensionality Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Due to the complexities of channel environments and the diversity of signal types, blind detection of communication signals in a non-cooperative communication environment remains a challenging problem. To alleviate these issues, we proposes a blind detection method for communication signals based on feature dimensionality reduction. Initially, multimodulus algorithm (MMA) is employed to eliminate the effects of the channel and a short time Fourier transform (STFT) is applied to generate a time-frequency representation. Furthermore, a combination of convolutional neural network (CNN) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) is utilized to extract common features that distinguish multiple types of signals from noise. This approach significantly enhances the algorithm's ability to extract features and improves detection rates. Experimental results demonstrate that, in a Rayleigh channel environment, with a false alarm rate of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and a signal-to-noise ratio of -10dB, the proposed algorithm achieves a detection rate of 94 %, which represents a notable improvement of approximately 10% compared to the STFT-CNN algorithm.

articleTitle: Slotted Microstrip Patch Antenna for Improved Sensing of Moisture Content in Leaf
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: The study of the molecular resistance against drought stress through the measurement of moisture content in leaf tissues leads to better plant management and breeding techniques. Implementation of a slotted patch antenna is presented for a non-destructive assessment of the moisture content of leaves at the resonant frequency of 2.80 GHz. The proposed antenna sensor is designed on an inexpensive F4B substrate having a thickness of 0.8 mm, dielelectric constant εr of 2.65, and a reduced dimension of 34.8 mm x 41.3 mm. Slots are employed above the feed line to miniaturize the size of the antenna. By positioning the wet leaf on a patch antenna sensor, the Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) is utlized to analyze the frequency variation in proportion to the moisture content. Subsequently, parametric analysis is carried out to demonstrate the actual behavior of the proposed technique with regard to the frequency of the designed antenna sensor. The dry and wet weight of the leaf are analyzed to determine the moisture content. The methodology is validated by the experimental results, which agree well with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Attentional Temporal Memory Fusion Network For Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification Under Low SNR
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: With the explosive growth of the number of internet of things (IoT) devices, the identity authentication of IoT devices has become a hot research direction of IoT communication security. Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) identification is an effective solution to the identity authentication of IoT devices, but its performance declines significantly at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). In this paper, a parallel multi-scale attentional temporal memory fusion network (MA-TMFN) is designed from the perspectives of feature extraction and feature fusion. The network extracts two scale features, global features and local features, and introduces an attentional feature fusion (AFF) module to assign different weights to the global and local features, so that the network can focus important multi-scale features of radio frequency (RF) signals in low SNR scenarios, thereby improving the RFF identification rate. Experiments were conducted with 18 IoT devices and the public automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast (ADS-B) dataset to evaluate the performance of MA-TMFN. Experimental results show that the proposed MA-TMFN performs better than other existing deep learning networks on different datasets at low SNR.

articleTitle: Two-Step Quantized Decoding for Block Markov Superposition Transmission of Fourier Transform Pair Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a two-step quantized decoding algorithm for the block Markov superposition transmission (BMST) system with Fourier transform pair (FTP) codes. The proposed algorithm aims to strike a balance among storage efficiency, computational complexity, and performance. In the first step, low-bit quantized information is used for iterative decoding, reducing storage space and computational complexity. In the second step, high-bit quantized information is employed to enhance overall performance. The simulation results demonstrate that the BMST-FTP system with two-step quantized decoding achieves comparable performance to high-bit quantization while maintaining low storage space and computational complexity. The proposed system offers a practical solution for efficient and high-performance BMST-FTP applications in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: A 0.06 mm2, 0.9 pJ/bit, 25 Gb/s Optical Receiver Front-End Module in 65 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper presents the measurement results of a 0.9 pJ/bit, 25-Gb/s optical receiver front-end based on the active-voltage current-feedback (AVCF) transimpedance amplifier (TIA). The proposed TIA core circuit has the stable operation and the increased gain compared with the conventional TIAs. The occupied chip area with I/O and DC pads is 660 μm x 580 μm (= 0.38 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and the proposed analog front-end TIA occupies only 360 μm x 160 μm (≈ 0.06 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The proposed module operates at 25-Gb/s with a supply voltage of 1.0 V and consumes only 22.6 mW.

articleTitle: A Low Computation Cost Model for Real-Time Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Developing speech enhancement systems for real-time scenarios has been a challenge due to the need for low computation complexity, parallel processing, and a causal structure. In this paper, we propose a speech enhancement model that works on time-frequency domain with all operations being 1D-dimensional to reduce computation cost. Specifically, the proposed model follows a U-Net structure with several conformer blocks inserted. Our evaluation on DNS Challenge and VoiceBank + DEMAND benchmarks shows that our model performs comparably to other state-of-the-art causal systems. Most importantly, the proposed model only needs 0.70G MACs when processing 16000 samples (1 second) speech signal and achieves an RTF (Real Time Factor) of 0.012, thus indicating that the model significantly reduces the computational cost.

articleTitle: A Distributed Spatial Reuse TDMA Slot Allocation Scheme Based on Topological Knowledge for UASNs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Modern ocean exploration missions rely on underwater acoustic networks, where are mainly charactered by a long propagation delay. An effective and efficient media access control protocol can improve the communication performance in underwater acoustic sensor networks. UASN is a type of underwater acoustic networks with random and almost stable topology. Therefore, we propose an algorithm, distributed spatial reuse time division multiple access (DSRTDMA), based on topological knowledge to adapt to this communication environment and provide better communication throughput. In this protocol, nodes utilize their two-hop topology and slot knowledge to achieve collision-free spatial reuse TDMA in a distributed slot allocation. Meanwhile, topological knowledge is also applied to effectively optimize the local TDMA slot allocation process. Finally, in simulation-based comparison with previous underwater acoustic protocols, our method performs best.

articleTitle: C2-DNSWatch: Endpoint Framework for Detecting Command and Control (C2) Connection of Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs)
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Advance Persistent Threats (APTs) are sophisti-cated cyber weapons for launching cyber offensive against adversaries. APTs implement state-of-the-art techniques and proceed in multiple stages to avoid detection. Apprehending APTs in developmental stages can lead to early discovery of attack. Command and Control (C2) connection is one of the essential stages of APTs and its timely discovery can lead to the detection of APTs. Most APTs employ Domain Name Service (DNS) as communication channels between attacker and victim. C2-DNSWatch, an endpoint framework has introduced an all-inclusive approach for detecting DNS-based C2 of APTs. It incorporates process-specific host-based features, correlated network activity, DNS metadata, DNS lexical analysis and threat intelligence from publicly available resources for detecting C2. Besides, it monitors the DNS link for probable data exfiltration. C2-DNSWatch has introduced many unique features, offering better performance and a high detection rate. C2-DNSWatch is an empirical framework for detecting C2 of APTs with an F1-Score of 98.70%.

articleTitle: Convolutional Auto-encoder-Based Packet-Loss-and-Error-Resilient Data Collection Method for Underwater Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In recent years, the underwater acoustic sensor network (UASN) is emerging as an effective means for marine data collection. However, due to the limited bandwidth of acoustic channel, the limited constrained energy supply of underwater sensors and data redundancy, it is impossible to deliver all the raw data generated by underwater sensors. Hence, to compress time-redundant data at a sensor node is of great significance for data collection from underwater sensors. Moreover, the underwater acoustic transmission link is unreliable, the issue of data collection with certain packet error resilience should be resolved. In this paper, a packet-loss-and-error-resilient data collection method based on convolutional auto-encoder (CAE) is proposed to collect the time-series data from underwater sensors, named as the PLER-CAE data collection method. In the proposed method, the auto-encoder is used to reduce data redundancy of the time-series data. The encoder deployed at the collection end compresses the data for transmission through the underwater channel, and the decoder deployed at the receiving end reconstructs the original data. Moreover, the proposed method complements the retransmission mechanism and the error correction technique in order to enhance data reconstruction quality. Numerical results show that the proposed PLER-CAE data collection method is effective.

articleTitle: Redundant multipath PQC key exchange using Shamir's Secret Sharing
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper proposes and evaluates multiple imple-mentations designed to fortify the security and resilience of a key exchange platform. Leveraging Shamir's Secret Sharing tech-nique, the system generates N sub-messages transmitted through disjoint network paths, preventing classical and quantum-enabled adversaries from reconstructing the original message without access to the requisite K sub-messages. Additionally, the inte-gration of Post-Quantum Cryptography, both before and after applying Shamir's Secret Sharing, employing Key Encapsulation Mechanisms for message encryption and signature algorithms for authentication, bolsters the platform's resilience against attacks on multiple networks. Successful attacks on either the Post-Quantum Cryptography or Shamir's Secret Sharing components in our implementation would not compromise the overall system security due to the two-factor approach. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the implemented system, achieving proficient key exchange rates under typical network traffic loads.

articleTitle: Pattern Synthesis of Dual-Polarized Conformal Array Based on Alternating Convex Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: A pattern synthesis of dual-polarized conformal arrays is proposed based on alternating convex optimization. The original beamforming problem is mathematically formulated as a joint optimization problem. However, the presence of both weight and auxiliary phase variables makes the problem non-convex. To address this issue, the non-convex problem is decomposed into two sub-problems, each targeting one variable. The sub-problem for optimizing the auxiliary phase is further transformed into a convex problem by using Taylor expansion. Then an alternating convex optimization approach is applied to iteratively solve the original problem. Furthermore, the “worst point” is identified based on the peak error in the main lobe region. Then the main lobe shaping performance is enhanced by increasing the weight at this point in the iterative process. The validity of method is confirmed by the result of the simulate experiment.

articleTitle: Implementation of High-Speed Multi-Trit Adders for Balanced and Unbalanced Ternary Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Ternary logic with larger data density has great potential in high-performance data processing. Even though ternary half/full adders have been intensively investigated in recent years, the high-speed multi-trit ternary adders, which are urgently needed for high-efficient ternary computing, remain unexplored. In this study, we present ternary carry lookahead adders (CLAs) to eliminate the tedious delay caused by the cascade-connected carry signals. Different implementation methods are used for unbalanced and balanced ternary logic. A delay analysis model of ternary CLAs is established. Compared with reported ternary carry ripple adders (CRAs), our 5-trit unbalanced and balanced ternary CLAs can achieve a 61.45% and 75.18% reduction in delay, respectively.

articleTitle: A Model Conversion Method Based on Unified CAE Data Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper investigates the method of reading and converting NASTRAN's BDF data file and Ansys' CDB data file into General software for marine structural analysis SAM's custom data format. NASTRAN and Ansys are two commonly used finite element analysis software, which have differences in data file formats, making it difficult to communicate their model data. To address this issue, this study designed and developed a conversion method that parses and processes BDF and CDB files to convert them into self-developed data formats. The paper focuses on the conversion methods of various data files, introduces the design and development of reading, parsing, and conversion methods, and verifies the system application through multiple experiments. This study is of great significance for promoting data sharing and collaboration among different finite element software. In the future, further exploration can be made on data conversion with other finite element software and the development of batch conversion tools.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Signal Denoising Method based on Improved Wavelet Threshold
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: To solve the distortion problem of the existing wavelet threshold denoising algorithm when processing electromagnetic signals, an SSA combined with an improved threshold function wavelet denoising algorithm is given. The improved wavelet threshold function has high-order derivability characteristics, which can overcome the problems of hard and soft threshold functions, and the SSA algorithm enhances the adaptivity of the wavelet denoising algorithm to different noises. The algorithm of this paper is applied to simulation experiments and electromagnetic compatibility measured data. The denoising algorithm in this paper improves the SNR by 54.81% and 17.85%, and reduces the RMSE by 54.57% and 29.06%, respectively, compared with the traditional hard and soft threshold denoising algorithms. The results show that the denoising effect is better than the existing wavelet threshold denoising algorithm.

articleTitle: A Wearable Multi-Sensor System for Flexible Wearing and Robust Monitoring of Muscle Activity
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Muscle activity monitoring plays a vital role in diverse fields, including clinical examination, rehabilitation assessment, and human-robotics interaction. However, the quality of acquired physiological signals often suffers due to limitations in sensor flexibility, robustness, and resistance to interference, which hampers the realization of long-term muscle activity monitoring. In this study, we introduced a novel wearable, flexible monitoring system, comprising a Magnetic-Inertial Measurement Unit (MIMU) and surface electromyography (sEMG) sensor. The designed flexible electrodes exhibited superior performance with low contact impedance and high signal-to-noise ratio. Additionally, we proposed an adaptive filtering algorithm based on a finite-state machine framework. This algorithm effectively compensated for orientation information by utilizing an electromagnetic interference observer and dynamically filtered electromyographic information through automated notch filter adjustments, enhancing the system's robustness against electromagnetic disturbances. Furthermore, validation experiments were conducted on five subjects across different muscle groups. The results, obtained from 12 hours of continuous monitoring with measurements taken every two hours, showcased consistent low contact impedance (60.32±12.15kΩ) and high signal-to-noise ratio (17.64±0.53 dB) of the designed flexible sensors. Notably, the system successfully improved posture-related information and dynamically filtered sEMG signals in environments with random magnetic field interference. In summary, our proposed flexible wearable monitoring system demonstrates promising capabilities in acquiring high-quality sEMG-orientation data, offering reliable and superiorquality information for applications in human-robot interaction.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient FPGA-Based Accelerator for Dynamic Sparse Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In recent years, transformer models have shown great potential in many fields of applications, including natural language processing and computer vision. To pursue better performance, transformer model size has become larger and larger which leads to a significant increase in computation complexity and memory intensity. All these factors make the transformer models challenging to be deployed in edge devices. To reduce the computation cost of transformer models, in this paper, an FPGA-based dynamic sparse attention accelerator is proposed for transformer model processing at the edge. The proposed accelerator is designed based on the fact that not all tokens in the self-attention are equally important. Accordingly, a low-precision prediction method by using dynamic mask is proposed to remove the sparse tokens in the self-attention module. In addition, an efficient Softmax computation method is proposed to reduce the memory requirement during Softmax computation. The proposed accelerator is implemented in the Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ device and improved speed performance and energy efficiency can be achieved when compared with previous designs.

articleTitle: A Low Power Multi-Bit Passive ΔΣ Modulator for Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: We present a low-power multi-bit passive ΔΣ modulator for wearable devices. Though delta-sigma modulators (DSM) that use passive filters can achieve low-power operation, the lower gain of the filters in those modulators causes lower resolution. Some techniques that exploit the combination of passive and active filters and low-gain circuits have been proposed to improve the resolution, which causes significant power dissipation. In this study, we propose a modulator that is composed of a passive filter and a 2-bit Flash ADC with a low-power comparator to overcome the above issues. We implemented the proposed modulator in a 0.18 μm CMOS technology, which has a bandwidth of 10 kHz for a clock frequency of 1.28 MHz. The circuit simulation results show that the proposed circuit achieves a maximum SNDR of 54 dB and a dynamic range of 62 dB with 1.75 μW power dissipation.

articleTitle: An Optimization for Mapping Orthogonal Polynomials Generation on CGRAs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In this paper, an optimization for mapping the generation of orthogonal polynomials on a specific CGRA is proposed for a research of the scalable Chiplet-based design. The method has been simulated with orthogonal polynomials in different orders upon various PEAs with comparable scales. The result shows that an average 1.9527×hardware resource utilization have been reached compared to scenarios without optimization.

articleTitle: A Robust Super-Resolution DoA Estimation Algorithm Using Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Direction of arrival (DoA) estimation is a fundamental problem in wireless communication and has received considerable attention. Most existing methods are lacking of the adaptation to some challenging observation conditions such as low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), limited number of snapshots and antenna array imperfections. To address these challenges, this paper presents a novel deep learning (DL) algorithm for DoA estimation, using the vision Transformer (ViT) for stronger global feature extraction capability. Specifically, we design a training label relying on the Gaussian distribution and integrate it into ViT to achieve superior DoA estimation precision. Furthermore, we use 1-bit quantized signals for simulation to verify the universality of our proposed algorithm. As the simulation results demonstrate, the proposed algorithm provides higher estimation accuracy and robustness in these challenging scenarios.

articleTitle: A Speech Enhancement Method Based on Dual-Path Phase-Aware GAN Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In the current research on speech enhancement, the estimation of the complex spectrum of clean speech from the noisy one, i.e., the real and imaginary parts, or the amplitude and phase, has become the mainstream in order to improve the intelligibility and perceptual quality of reconstructed speech. The accuracy of phase estimation has been limited due to phase unwrapping. To address this problem, this paper proposes a dual-path GAN structure. In this structure, one path is dedicated to estimate the amplitude of speech spectrum, and the other path focuses on the phase part. At the same time, those two paths undergo information interaction, which improves the accuracy of the amplitude estimation and phase estimation. Also, we propose a novel phase loss function, which focus on stable phase estimation maintaining phase continuity. Simulation results show that the performance of the proposed speech enhancement algorithm has been significantly improved, which verifies the effectiveness of the method in this paper.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis for Uplink NOMA System Based on Hybrid SIC Decoding Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In this paper, based on an uplink two users NOMA (non-orthogonal multiple access) system, a hybrid SIC (successive interference cancelation) decoding strategy is proposed, in which BS (base station) adaptively select SIC decoding strategy according to channel station information (CSI) and QoS (quality of service) constrains. As we all know, determining the user's SIC decoding order based on QoS and CSI, have their own shortcomings, respectively. However, the proposed hybrid SIC decoding strategy can effectively overcome the shortcomings of the above two traditional strategies. Monte-Carlo simulations show that the hybrid SIC decoding strategy obtain better performance compared to two traditional strategies (CSI SIC decoding strategy and QoS SIC decoding strategy) and OMA (orthogonal multiple access) transmission mode. In addition, we also can see that, the power allocation coefficient has important impact on the ergodic capacity and outage probability of Un (near-end user) based on two traditional strategies. However, based on hybrid SIC decoding strategy, the change of the power allocation coefficient has little effect on the performance of Un. This shows that the proposed hybrid SIC decoding strategy has good robustness to the change of the power allocation coefficient.

articleTitle: A Study on a Code Assisted Based Blind Timing Synchronization Technique for Short Data Packets
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Short packets based on Cyclic Code Shift Keying (CCSK) can eliminate the pilot synchronization sequence overhead and effectively improve the transmission efficiency of short packets, however, its timing synchronization accuracy performs poorly at low SNR, this paper proposes a CCSK short packet based on Non-Binary Low Density Parity Check Code (NB-LDPC) blind timing synchronization scheme. The scheme utilizes the check matrix of NB-LDPC to construct the objective function, and the total number of accumulated objective functions satisfying the check matrix is used as the synchronization metric criterion to achieve the estimation of the CCSK short packet code-slice level timing error. Simulation results show that for the short packet blind synchronization system, the NB-LDPC-based code-assisted synchronization is more effective and significantly improves the system performance at low signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: Enhanced DSP Blocks for Full High-Definition Video Bridging Application on FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: FPGA chips are widely used in video bridging applications. The DSP (Digital Signal Processing) in FPGA can effectively improve the efficiency of video image processing algorithms. The 10 bits of pixel depth is common for Full High-Definition (FHD). However, in the existing commercial FPGAs, the DSP does not naturally support 10x10 multiplication. This brings some waste in area and power consumption. This paper proposes a new architecture of embedded DSP. It increases the maximum number of 10x10 multiplications in a DSP block to 8. It is also compatible with common working modes such as multiplication (18x18, 18x9), and accumulation. Meanwhile, introduce power gate and clock gate units in the DSP block to achieve fine-grained control of the power consumption. Users can dynamically control the power supply through their own logic. The entire circuit was successfully designed and implemented in an industrial 22nm process. The experimental results show that the static power consumption of the DSP block is about 20uW, the dynamic power consumption is about 200uW. And the maximum operating frequency can reach 670MHz. The effective area utilization of our DSP in 10x10 mode is 2.2 and 2.5 times higher than that in Intel Arria 10 series and Xilinx UltraScale series FPGAs, respectively.

articleTitle: Intelligent Prediction Model for Ship Roll Damping Based on CTGAN-XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In order to prevent the substantial rolling of ships in intricate and harsh marine environments, ensuring the safety of personnel and cargo during maritime transportation, this paper proposes an intelligent prediction model for ship roll damping based on CTGAN-XGBoost. Firstly, a dataset for roll damping is constructed using ship geometry model data and ship motion data to improve data quality. Then, a Conditional Table Generative Adversarial Network is used to balance and generate more roll damping data, thereby augmenting the quantity of available data. Finally, taking advantage of XGBoost's strong generalization ability and low overfitting degree, an intelligent prediction model for roll damping is established. Experimental results demonstrate that the CTGAN-XGBoost model achieves the highest accuracy with MSE and MAE values of only 0.325 and 0.451 respectively, along with an R2 value of 0.975. It significantly outperforms other comparative models in terms of predictive accuracy.

articleTitle: Efficient FPGA-Based Transformer Accelerator Using In-Block Balanced Pruning
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Recently, transformer models have been widely deployed in natural language processing and image processing. However, its superior performance comes with high amount of parameters and computations which make it difficult to deploy transformer models in resource limited devices. To reduce the computation cost of transformer models, in this paper, an improved network pruning method is proposed. In the proposed pruning method, the parameter matrix is decomposed into blocks of a specific size. Then, pruning is applied to each block so that the number of parameters remaining in each block is the same. To further reduce the memory requirement of the parameters, an efficient memory storage pattern for sparse parameters is also proposed in this paper. Finally, by combining the proposed methods, an energy efficient transformer accelerator architecture is proposed. The proposed accelerator is implemented in FPGA devices and implementation results show that the proposed design can significantly improve the speed performance and energy efficiency when compared with previous designs.

articleTitle: A Dual-Mode Split-Based Calibration Technique for Time-Interleaved ADCs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper proposes a structure of spilt ADC which can be converted to a Time interleaved (TI) sampling mode to double the sampling rate. The architecture has two modes. In the split mode, two channels use the same clock, and through the split architecture the capacitor mismatch error, amplifier gain error, and timing skew are calibrated. After calibrate those nonideal factors, the TI mode is started. By shifting the phase of one clock 180-degree, the sampling rate is doubled. The architecture greatly reduces the complexity of the calibration algorithm and hardware consumption of time-interleaved ADC. The behavioral simulation shows llbit split ADC can be converted to TI ADC with double sampling rate which achieves 58dB SNDR, 78dB SFDR on average.

articleTitle: Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection Based on Time-Frequency Dynamic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of internet of things and big data technologies, there is a growing demand for accurate and efficient in processing and analysis of extensive time series data in various application scenarios. However, traditional anomaly detection methods ineffective in large-scale, high-dimensional,and dynamically changing time series data. In response to this challenge, this paper proposes a novel time series anomaly detection method that integrates the dynamic graph at-tention mechanism with time-frequency domain feature analysis. This integration enhances the model's sensitivity to temporal and frequency-related data changes, allowing it to capture intricate spatial dependencies within time series. Moreover, by conducting a comprehensive analysis of time and frequency domain features, the proposed method named TFAD-GAT, which reveals profound patterns and detects abnormal behaviors concealed within the data. Compared with traditional methods, this method improves the accuracy, recall and Fl score of anomaly detection in the SMD dataset, and the recall and Fl score in the SWaT dataset.

articleTitle: A Centralized Block Placement Algorithm Based on Sequence Pair Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In the field of Electronic Design Automation (EDA), particularly in Printed Circuit Board (PCB) design, the placement of blocks is a very important issue. Superior PCB designs implement a placement strategy centered around key blocks such as processors, memory, and power management blocks. Designers arrange auxiliary blocks and connections around these core blocks to ensure logical clarity, effective signal transmission, and minimal interference. Research on a centralized block placement algorithm based on sequence pairs has been conducted in this paper, extracting the positional relationships between the central block and other blocks from the sequence pairs. On this basis, this paper proposes a new sequence pair initialization method and perturbation strategy, and also studies a modified version of the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) algorithm. Through testing several examples in the industry, the experimental results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper can achieve centralized placement. Block placement is actually a common scientific problem in the field of EDA, so that the centralized block placement algorithm proposed in this paper can be applied not only to PCB design but also to the problem of VLSI placement.

articleTitle: Optimal Navigation for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Based on Improved A * Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: The growing need of ocean surveying and exploration in maritime application has led to the requirement of optimal path planning strategies for ocean vehicles. The A * algorithm is the most used algorithm in practice for calculating a path with the shortest distance cost. However, the path generated by the conventional A * algorithm is constrained by the grid map and it may not be compatible with the vehicle's motion. An improved A * algorithm is proposed in this paper. A new weight heuristic function is proposed that considers the effect of the safe distance from obstacles. And a line-of-sight based algorithm is used to smooth the paths, which improves the path performance and reduces unnecessary jags. Simulation results show that the improved A * algorithm out performs the conventional algorithm in both safety and practicability.

articleTitle: A Permutation Dispatch Circuit Design for Quantum Permutation Pad Symmetric Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Quantum Permutation Pad (QPP) is a symmetric-key quantum block data encryption scheme. Central to QPP is using value permutations in the encryption and decryption procedures. A plaintext is encrypted with a sequence of randomly selected permutations and decrypted by their inverses. Implementing QPP requires a random dispatching operation determining the permutation operators used for encryption. The efficient implementation of the dispatching operation remains an open question. We propose an efficient solution to the dispatching operation. A detailed circuit design is presented, analyzed, and implemented.

articleTitle: Development of a Universal Vacuum Acquisition System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This paper introduces a four channels vacuum acquisition system based on LPC1788 main control, which can be widely used in the vacuum gauge of INFICON and other companies. The system uses the vacuum gauge as the sensor, conducts signal processing with the help of OPA4277, and use AD7689 to perform analog-to-digital transformation, while through SPI to communicate with the chip. The system supports two communication modes, including RS232 and Bluetooth, which enables flexible and reliable data transmission. Through detailed system design and experimental verification, the paper fully proves the feasibility and effectiveness of the system in the field of vacuum acquisition.

Author Keywords: analog signal and digital signal processing

articleTitle: Beamspace Channel Estimation via Atomic Norm Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Beamspace Massive multiple-input multiple-output (Massive MIMO) based on lens antenna arrays (LAAs) has shown significant potential to provide high data rate as it can achieve sufficient beamforming gain with a limited number of radio frequency (RF) chains. However, channel estimation is extremely challenging due to the transceiver architecture with few RF chains and a large number of antennas. Most existing beamspace channel estimation schemes are grid-based sparse signal reconstruction. Although compressed sensing (CS) can guarantee the reconstruction performance for signals located on the grid, it cannot perfectly map all true signals onto the grid due to its continuous nature, which leads to the basis mismatch problem, and thus reduces the estimation performance. To this end, in this paper we investigate a continuous dictionary for beamspace channel estimation. Specifically, the beamspace channel estimation is formulated as an atomic norm minimization (ANM) problem. On this basis, a continuous dictionary is employed for channel angle estimation to avoid the effects of base mismatch caused by grid-based CS methods. The effectiveness of the proposed ANM estimation method is verified by the simulation results, as the proposed scheme outperforms the existing CS-based grid estimation methods.

articleTitle: Minimum Strong Radius of the Strong Product of Cycles and Even Paths
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In interconnection networks, the efficiency of information transmission depends on the length of the transmission path. Typically, we use radius as a metric to evaluate the information transmission performance of undirected networks; however, this metric is not applicable to directed networks. In a strongly directed graph, the strong distance between any two vertices is defined as the minimum directed strong subgraph of the strong directed graph containing these two vertices, the strong centrality of a vertex is defined as the maximum of the strong distances from that vertex to the other vertices, and the strong radius of the strong directed graph is defined as the minimum of the strong centrality of all the vertices. The minimum strong radius as the minimum of the strong radius of all strong directed graphs of the graph is an important metric for evaluating and optimizing the performance of information transmission in directed networks. In this paper, we construct a strong product network of cycles and even paths, and determine the exact value of the minimum strong radius of the strong product network of cycles and even paths when the length of the cycles is greater than or equal to 3 and greater than the length of the even paths. In addition, we give upper and lower bounds on the minimum strong radius of the strong product network of cycles and even paths when the length of the cycle is greater than or equal to 4 and less than or equal to the length of the even path.

articleTitle: MoSK Modulation-Assisted RRNS Coding Scheme in Molecular Diffusion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In this paper, we applied (k+1, k) redundant residue number system (RRNS) codes, assisted by molecule shift keying (MoSK) modulation technology, to molecular diffusion systems (MDS). A (k + 1, k) RRNS code consists of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> information residues and one redundant residue. Using a simple algebraic check algorithm, the (k +1, k) RRNS code has the ability to correct a single symbol error resulting from a single bit error in error space. One of the advantages of the proposed approach in this study is that it requires fewer molecular types and still achieves improved decoding performance compared to the approach using MoSK modulation only. In addition, the algebraic features of the RRNS encoding and decoding algorithms reduce the computational complexity. The bit error rate (BER) simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MDS system. Furthermore, the proposed approach has the potential to be implemented in other types of molecular communication.

articleTitle: A Global Router with Topology Optimization on Hanan Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Global routing not only becomes an essential part in the domain of EDA backend routing but also serves as a method to quickly assess routing resources. Also, it dominates propelling and guiding detailed routing. Unluckily, minimization of overflow on PCB boards remains more challenging for a great maj ority of global routing algorithms due to the flexibility of PCB routing and the complexity of net topology. A novel global routing approach is put forward here at this point. Its process involves establishing a Hanan grid to represent spatial resources, applying the A * algorithm with rip-up and reroute for congestion negotiation. Meanwhile, a topology optimization model is introduced to explore more optimal topologies for minimization of overflow. Our measurements indicate that our global routing approach can achieve higher routing rate in less time in comparison with other global routing methods.

articleTitle: Underwater Passive Target Detection Based on Sub-Band Peak Modified Energy and Number Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Beamforming with post-processing methods are widely used for underwater target detection through the uniform linear array. By employing the minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming with diagonal loading, the bearing time recorder (BTR) can be obtained, but usually contains sidelobe and noise, which is not beneficial to target detection. Although the sub-band peak energy detection (SPED) brings a raise of the resolution and a reduction to most of the noise and sidelobe, it may also increase the strong sidelobe and cause significant false alarm. In order to improve the detection performance and further utilize spatial continuity of beam scanning azimuth spectrums, an underwater passive target detection algorithm based on sub-band peak modified energy and number filtering is proposed. After selecting the peaks by SPED and applying the Eckart filtering to raise the signal-to-noise ratio, a joint selection of azimuths according to the peak accumulated energy and number is put forward, and only the peaks at the azimuths where the targets are probably located are preserved. Compared to the SPED, the sidelobe could be removed through the proposed work, which results in lower false alarm rate and improved detection performance of weak targets.

articleTitle: Integrated Optical Fiber Sensor for Temperature-Compensated Refractive Index Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: An innovative integrated fiber optic sensor has been proposed for accurate detection of refractive index (RI) variations in the test solution, utilizing temperature compensation. This sensor employs a detection mechanism combining Fabry-Perot Interferometry (FPI) and Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR), achieving high sensitivity refractive index measurements with temperature compensation. SPR is excited by depositing a metal film on the fiber surface, enabling detection of external solution refractive index variations. Additionally, the presence of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) in the structure enables temperature compensation, effectively correcting the influence of temperature changes on the measured refractive index of the test liquid. The test results demonstrate that the SPR sensitivity to refractive index and temperature are 1875.20 nm/RIU and -0.12 nm/°C, respectively. The FPI exhibits a temperature sensitivity of -0.61 nm/°C. By constructing a sensitivity matrix, simultaneous measurement of the refractive index of the test solution and temperature compensation are achieved. This study presents a compact temperature-compensated plug-in physical sensor for detecting the refractive index of the test solution. It is a small-sized, user-friendly, and cost-effective sensor suitable for various applications, including environmental monitoring, industrial process control, medical diagnosis, and liquid measurement.

articleTitle: A New Transmission Scheme: Semi-Blind Channel Estimation Combined with Precoding
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In this paper, we first introduce the transmission model of MIMO-OFDM. A semi blind estimation method based on noise subspace is proposed to overcome some limitations of blind estimation methods. Then a new transmission scheme is proposed, in which the channel information obtained by blind or semi blind estimation will be used for the precoder. At the end of this paper, the performance of this data transmission scheme is analyzed and discussed, and the parameters, especially the size of the data frame, can be adjusted according to the needs, which can affect the transmission efficiency and delay. Adjusting parameters according to channel conditions and communication requirements is crucial for optimizing the efficiency and robustness of transmission systems.

articleTitle: DCE-CDPPTnet: Dense Connected Encoder Cross Dual-Path Parrel Transformer Network for Multi-Channel Speech Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In recent years, there has been increasing attention given to the end-to-end time domain model for speech separation task, which has demonstrated superior performance. Specifically, research in time domain speech separation has focused on two main areas: extracting more effective features and improving the modeling of temporal speech sequences. To tackle these challenges, we propose the dense connected encoder cross dual-path parallel transformer network (DCE-CDPPTnet) for multi-channel speech separation. By utilizing a dense connected encoder, our network is able to enhance feature extraction through multilayer convolutional layers organized by dense connected structure. Furthermore, this encoder also mitigates the issue of gradient disappearance. In order to better model long-time speech sequences, our proposed model incorporates the cross dual-path parallel transformer. This transformer utilizes both the intra improved transformer and the inter improved transformer to capture local and global information, respectively. Moreover, the CDPPTnet enables local information and global information can interact by parallelizing the intra improved transformer and the inter improved transformer. Simulation results under various model configurations, demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed DCE-CDPPTnet compared to the filter-and-sum network with transform-average-concatenate module (FaSNet-TAC).

articleTitle: Microsphere Sensitized Fiber Optic SPR Biosensor for Refractive Index Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In this paper, barium titanate glass microspheres were combined with optical fiber microspheres to enhance the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effect of the optical fiber microspheres probe, and a probe type optical fiber sensor for detection was developed. The sensor adopts a reflective structure; the light source enters the tip of the probe by a single-mode fiber to stimulate the SPR effect and then returns through the single-mode fiber, and a spectrometer monitors the change of the reflected signal. Firstly, COMSOL Multiphysics was used for simulation to verify the sensitization effect of structure optimization using barium titanate microspheres at the theoretical level. To verify the actual detection effect of the sensor, this paper uses different concentrations of sodium chloride solution for refractive index detection experiments. It makes two kinds of fiber optic sensors for comparative experiments before and after structure optimization. The experimental results show that the refractive index sensitivity of the structure before and after optimization using barium titanate microspheres is 2486 nm/RIU and 6802 nm/RIU, respectively. Combined with different functionalization methods, the sensor can be used to detect a variety of parameters. Through the chemical modification of the gold film on the sensor's surface, the detection markers were captured on the surface of the microspheres, resulting in local refractive index changes, and the qualitative and quantitative detection of different parameters was realized. Alternatively, there is great potential in diagnosing major diseases by detecting the concentrations of specific biomarkers.

articleTitle: A 4-to-16GHz Dual-Loop PLL Based on Current-Control RO and Calibration in a 6-nm FinFET
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: This work presents a PLL design in an advanced 6- nm FinFET CMOS technology and proposes a strategy for designing a ring-based PLL with low jitter and reference spur performance. With calibration function, the ring-based PLL achieves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$420-\text{fs}_{\text{rms}}$</tex> integrated jitter and reference spurs at -68 dBc, which can meet the low noise requirements of 32Gbps SerDes. The PLL has an active area of 0.015 mm2, consuming 4.9 mW from a 0.75V supply at 16GHz, translating to a figure of merit of -240.6 dB.

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic FBMC System Based on Dual Prototype Filters and Pruned-DFT
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: The complex and changeable characteristics of the underwater acoustic channels reduce the performance of the underwater acoustic (UWA) communication. High peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and bit error rate (BER) performance are main problems in UWA communications. To address above issues, the pruned discrete Fourier transform (Pruned-DFT) of filter bank multicarrier (FBMC) scheme in UWA is introduced, which can decrease the PAPR. We also propose dual filters based on sequence (DFBS), and random binary sequence allows the prototype filter to be used flexibly without increasing the complexity of the system. At the same time, in order to reduce the intrinsic interference, auxiliary orthogonalization matrix is employed to improve BER performance of the system. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can effectively reduce BER and PAPR of the system.

articleTitle: Joint Resource Allocation and Task Scheduling for UAV-Assisted ISCC Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: Integrated sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC) shows great potential in future wireless networks. In this paper, we investigate a UAV-assisted ISCC system with mobile edge computing (MEC) servers, where the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) device deployed on the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) provides sensing target service and communication services to user, simultaneously. Specifically, the UAV collects sensing data and determines the scheduling strategy for computing sensing tasks between local computation and partial offloading to edge server (ES), while maintaining the communication link with the user. Our aim is to satisfy the radar sensing performance based on the trade-off of resource allocation among sensing, communication, and computation as well as task scheduling to minimize the system delay. We formulate the joint optimization problem of UAV transmission power, and offloading ratio to minimize the system delay, which is nonconvex and difficult to solve. Then, we propose a decoupled approximation algorithm (DAA) that decomposes the formulated problem into two subproblems. We use the Lagrange multiplier method and the mathematical theoretical method to jointly optimize the power allocation and the offloading ratio to obtain a near-optimal solution of the formulated problem. Extensive simulation validation shows that our proposed algorithm not only ensures the radar sensing quality, but also significantly reduces the system delay.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Vector Perturbation Precoding with Projection Analysis Assisted Subspace Searching
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel low-complexity vector perturbation (VP) precoding is presented for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems with projection analysis (PA) assisted subspace searching method as VP-PA. It is verified with the projection analysis in this paper that if the perturbed transmit signal vector is in the subspaces spanned by the right singular vector with the least singular value of its precoding matrix, the transmit signal power is reduced to a shortest projection sum. Therefore, the conventional full searching space for VP method is significantly shrunk in the above subspaces to reduce the complexity. However, the best perturbation vector to fall in the above subspaces can't always be an integer perturbation vector, thus our approach involves searching integer perturbation vector in the shrunk subspaces to minimize the transmit power and reduce the complexity. The complexity and performance of the proposed VP-PA are analyzed and compared with conventional VP methods, which is proved to be a good choice for VP method considering both the performance and complexity.

articleTitle: Prediction of Ship Propulsion Power based on Bayesian optimized LightGBM Using Ship In-Service Data
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: In maritime operations, accurate prediction and control of the propulsion power of the ship's main engine are crucial, as they directly impact the fuel economy, speed performance and carbon emission control. To enhance prediction accuracy, this paper proposes a regression prediction method for ship propulsion power based on the LightGBM model, specifically designed for vessels equipped with air lubrication drag reduction systems. First, domain knowledge is used to select sensor monitoring data related to main engine propulsion power, preprocess it as input variables, and use main engine propulsion power as output. Bayesian optimization is then used to adjust the hyper-parameters of the model. Finally, in order to evaluate the performance of this method, comparisons are made with multiple linear regression and support vector machine (SVM) regression in predicting ship propulsion power. The results show that the LightGBM model based on Bayesian optimization has strong generalization ability, short training time and superior performance.

articleTitle: A Software and Hardware Design for Buoy Based Marine Data Acquisition System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: The ocean observation buoy, as a floating automated monitoring platform, plays a crucial role in monitoring ocean meteorological, hydrological, and ecological parameters in marine research. In response to the issues of poor performance, accuracy, and reliability in observation buoys, this article proposes a multi-parameter ocean-atmosphere buoy data acquisition system. The design involves multi-dimensional data collection, data transmission methods, and low power consumption in the buoy. First, the system employs high-performance sensors for accurate data collection. Second, it utilizes the BeiDou satellite for remote communication and controls the system using an embedded STM32 low-power module. Third, an acquisition control program is developed based on LabView software. Experimental validation demonstrates that the system can effectively measure various parameters in the marine meteorological environment, such as temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind speed, and wind direction.

articleTitle: Design Implementation and Verification of a Flexible I3C Hardware Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: The emergence of the Improved Inter-Integrated Circuit (I3C) protocol has led to a proliferation of products featuring I3C interfaces in the market. However, existing I3C devices often suffer from limited compatibility and adaptability. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a flexible hardware architecture specifically designed for I3C. The architecture is built upon configurable and reusable components integrated within the hardware design, enabling upper-layer software to dynamically adjust the behavior and functionality of the I3C interface via hardware registers. This approach effectively meets the diverse requirements of I3C peripheral device chips. After a comprehensive design and functional verification, the developed I3C module is confirmed to operate correctly, achieving a code coverage of 99.02% and functional coverage of 100%.

articleTitle: Class AB Power Amplifier with A Differential Cold-FET Pre-Distorter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems (ICCCAS)
abstract: A two stage class AB power amplifier (PA) for the frequency range 24–30 GHz is proposed. The PA relies on a cold-FET connected in a differential configuration to enhance the amplitude to amplitude modulation (AM-AM) distortion. In addition, a capacitor is added to improve the amplitude to phase modulation (AM-PM) distortion. Post-layout simulations using the 65nm CMOS technology node show an output 1dB compression point (OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf>) higher by 1.8 dB and its power added efficiency (PAE) increases by 3.1 % when compared to the PA without using the proposed differential cold-FET technique. The proposed PA achieves a gain of 18 dB with an AM-PM of 1.3°. The peak saturated power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>) is 16.5 dBm, with a peak PAE of 21.7%.

articleTitle: Ship and Ocean Visual Simulation System Based on High Definition Render Pipeline
